title: Adding gas under a piston
hook: Change one condition and watch the gas respond.

knows: A gas has pressure, volume, temperature and an amount.
doesNotKnow: At fixed temperature and pressure, gas volume is proportional to amount. Doubling the amount doubles volume from 1 L to 2 L.

misconception: Changing one gas variable always leaves the others unchanged.
objective: Use the ideal gas law with the stated fixed conditions.

claims.text: Question, chart and reveal: An ideal gas occupies 1 L. The gas amount doubles while temperature and pressure remain fixed. What is its final volume? At fixed temperature and pressure, gas volume is proportional to amount. Doubling the amount doubles volume from 1 L to 2 L.
claims.source: PV = nRT under the stated fixed conditions; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/9-summary

claims.text: Dots are schematic and not individual real gas molecules; the piston is an idealized representation and the model does not predict deviations from ideal behavior.
Recall: At fixed temperature and pressure, what happens to ideal-gas volume if gas amount doubles? Volume is proportional to amount at fixed temperature and pressure.

recall.question: At fixed temperature and pressure, what happens to ideal-gas volume if gas amount doubles?
recall.why: Volume is proportional to amount at fixed temperature and pressure.
